_provenance: Cross-implementation AES-256-GCM fixture for plan U3 (docs/plans/2026-08-03-001-feat-reactions-attachments-parity-plan.md). The plan asks for a ciphertext fixture produced by pacto-app's own encrypt path. A pacto-app checkout exists on this development machine (~/src/covenant-gov/pacto-app) but its working tree carries uncommitted changes from concurrent work on another plan, so it was read only -- src-tauri/src/crypto.rs:68-93 (encrypt_data) was inspected to confirm the byte layout this fixture exercises: AesGcm::<Aes256, U16>::new, encrypt_in_place_detached, then the 16-byte tag appended to the ciphertext -- and was not built, to avoid disturbing that concurrent work. This vector is instead produced by an INDEPENDENT AES-256-GCM implementation: Python's `cryptography` package (OpenSSL-backed), not the `aes-gcm` Rust crate under test, so the round trip in tests/attachment_crypto.rs is a genuine cross-implementation check rather than a same-crate proof. Exact generation commands: `python3 -m venv /tmp/attfixture_venv && /tmp/attfixture_venv/bin/pip install cryptography` (installed cryptography==50.0.0), then: `/tmp/attfixture_venv/bin/python3 -c "import json, secrets; from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM; key = secrets.token_bytes(32); nonce = secrets.token_bytes(16); plaintext = b'pacto attachment fixture: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 0123456789'; ct = AESGCM(key).encrypt(nonce, plaintext, None); print(json.dumps({'key_hex': key.hex(), 'nonce_hex': nonce.hex(), 'plaintext_hex': plaintext.hex(), 'ciphertext_hex': ct.hex()}))"`. AESGCM.encrypt with a 16-byte nonce and no associated data returns ciphertext || tag, exactly the layout attachment::crypto::encrypt must produce.
